name: Issue: Feature request: post-command hook event for extension commands (https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/1782)

{"assignees":[],"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjEzOTI=","is_bot":false,"login":"bcotton","name":"Bob Cotton"},"body":"## Problem

There is currently no event that fires after an extension command (registered via `pi.registerCommand()`) completes. This makes it impossible for one extension to react to another extension's command completing.

## Concrete use case: push-line extension

A [zsh-style push-line](https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Zsh-Line-Editor.html#index-push_002dline) extension stores the current editor text on a stack (via `Alt+Q`) so the user can run a quick command, then automatically restores the stashed text when that command finishes.

For **regular LLM prompts** this works fine: `agent_end` fires after the agent loop completes and the extension restores the editor text via `ctx.ui.setEditorText()`.

For **slash commands** (e.g. `/task`, `/model`, any `registerCommand` handler) the restore cannot happen automatically because:

- Extension commands are checked first and **bypass** the `input` event entirely (per the lifecycle docs)
- `agent_end` never fires because the agent loop is never entered
- There is no other event in the system that fires after a command handler returns

The extension currently works around this with a manual `/pop-line` command the user must remember to call after every slash command. That's a poor UX compared to the seamless automatic restore that works for LLM prompts.

## Proposed solution

Add a new lifecycle event — e.g. `command_end` (or `command_complete`) — that fires after any extension command handler resolves:

```typescript
pi.on("command_end", async (event, ctx) => {
  // event.name      — the command name (e.g. "task")
  // event.args      — the raw argument string passed to the command
  // event.duration  — ms the handler took (optional but useful)
});
```

A symmetric `command_start` event would also be useful for telemetry/tracing extensions.

## Why this matters beyond push-line

Any extension that needs to react to *any* user interaction — whether it results in an agent run or not — currently cannot. Examples:

- **Telemetry/tracing extensions** (like `tempo-tracer.ts`) that want to record a span for every user action, not just agent runs
- **Session-state extensions** that update a status widget after any command changes state
- **Undo/checkpoint extensions** that want to snapshot before every interaction regardless of type

The current event surface makes the agent loop a first-class citizen but treats slash commands as a blind spot.","closed":false,"comments":[],"labels":[],"milestone":null,"number":1782,"projectItems":[],"state":"OPEN","title":"Feature request: post-command hook event for extension commands","url":"https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/1782"}
